module_title: Mechanics of Satellites: Orbital Velocity and Geostationary Orbits
introduction: Satellites are celestial or artificial bodies that revolve around a planet. The physics behind placing rockets and communication satellites in space relies on a delicate balance between gravitational pull and orbital speed.

core_concepts.title: Orbital Velocity ($v_o$)
core_concepts.description:
The minimum velocity required to put a satellite into its orbit around the Earth. 
Formula: $v_o = \sqrt{gR}$. 
For a satellite orbiting very close to the Earth's surface, the orbital velocity is approximately $7.92 \text{ km/s} \approx 8 \text{ km/s}$.

core_concepts.title: Relation between Escape and Orbital Velocity
core_concepts.description:
Formula: $v_e = \sqrt{2} v_o$. 
If the orbital velocity of a satellite is increased by $41.4\%$ (which is $\sqrt{2}$ times), it will leave its orbit and escape into outer space.

core_concepts.title: Geostationary Satellites
core_concepts.description:
These are communication satellites that appear 'Stationary' (fixed) in the sky when observed from the Earth. 
Conditions: 
1. Height must be exactly '$36,000 \text{ km}$' above the Earth's surface. 
2. Their time period of revolution must be exactly equal to the Earth's rotation (24 hours). 
3. They must revolve from 'West to East' in an orbit coplanar with the Equator.

core_concepts.title: Polar Satellites
core_concepts.description: These satellites revolve around the Earth in a North-South direction, passing over the poles. They orbit at lower altitudes ($700-800 \text{ km}$). They are used for weather forecasting, spying, and remote sensing mapping.

important_entities.name: Weightlessness in Space
important_entities.significance: Astronauts inside a space station feel 'Weightless' because both the astronaut and the satellite are in a continuous state of 'Free fall' toward the Earth. The normal reaction force of the floor is zero.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: Satellites do NOT need fuel to orbit
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A massive misconception: 'Satellites need to burn fuel continuously to stay in orbit.' FALSE. Once a satellite achieves its orbital velocity ($v_o$), it requires NO fuel to keep moving forward. The Earth's gravity provides the necessary centripetal force to bend its path into a circle.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Always remember that Geostationary satellites are parked exactly at 36,000 km altitude. This specific number is tested countless times in State PCS and NDA.

exam_strategy_tips: For UPSC/State PCS: Differentiate between their uses. Geostationary = Telecommunications (DTH, TV, Phones). Polar = Weather prediction and Earth observation (cameras).
